problem: Deploying compute-heavy Vision-Language-Action models on resource-constrained mobile robots is hard, and monolithic end-to-end fine-tuned VLMs overfit to training scenarios and fail to generalize to novel objects.
motivation: VLAs promise to link high-level semantic intent to low-level control, but edge deployment needs low latency and open-world generalization. The observation is that a fine-tuned monolithic LVLM works in trained scenarios but overfits, suggesting reasoning, perception and control should be separated.
key_idea: Decouple language understanding (Small Language Model for intent extraction) from perception (open-vocabulary detector for visual grounding) and control (lightweight MLP policy) for crawler robot navigation, instead of a monolithic end-to-end fine-tuned LVLM.
insight: Per the abstract, the monolithic fine-tuned LVLM is highly effective in trained scenarios but overfits and fails on novel objects, while the modular design gets better zero-shot generalization and lower latency. Disentangling semantic understanding from control lets the open-vocabulary detector supply open-world generalization and keeps the learned policy small. Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited.
method: Monolithic baseline: fine-tune a Large Vision-Language Model to map visual observations directly to control commands.
Intent extraction: a Small Language Model parses the natural-language instruction into the target intent.
Visual grounding: an Open-Vocabulary Detector localizes the target object in the camera image.
Control policy: a lightweight MLP maps the grounded detection to crawler robot control commands.

setting.backbone: Fine-tuned Large VLM (monolithic baseline); Small Language Model + Open-Vocabulary Detector + MLP policy (modular)
setting.training_data: Not stated in abstract (fine-tuning data for the LVLM and training data for the MLP policy)
setting.action_space: Low-level control commands for a crawler robot

results: The modular approach is reported to achieve superior zero-shot generalization and lower inference latency than the monolithic fine-tuned LVLM baseline, which overfits and fails on novel objects. No quantitative numbers are given in the abstract.
limitations: Evidence limited to a single crawler robot platform and a comparison of two architectures (per abstract).
Modular pipeline depends on the detector's vocabulary and on the accuracy of the SLM's intent extraction.
